arxiv-2012-10268.title: Gate-Based Circuit Designs For Quantum Adder Inspired Quantum Random Walks on Superconducting Qubits
arxiv-2012-10268.creator: Daniel Koch 1 ∗ , Michael Samodurov 2 , Andrew Projansky 3 , Paul M. Alsing 1
arxiv-2012-10268.description: Abstract Quantum Random Walks, which have drawn much attention over the past few decades for their distinctly non-classical behavior, is a promising subfield within Quantum Computing. Theoretical framework and applications for these walks have seen many great mathematical advances, with experimental demonstrations now catching up.

arxiv-2112-05252.title: Polyhedral Analysis of a Polytope from a Service Center Location Problem with a Type of Decision-Dependent Customer Demand Journal: Discrete Applied Mathematics
arxiv-2112-05252.creator: Fengqiao Luo
arxiv-2112-05252.description: Abstract The polytope from a service center location problem with a special location-dependent demand has been investigated in this paper. The location-dependent demand is defined based on a maximum-attraction-principle assumption. Along this direction, the intersection polytope of the capacity constraints and demand constraints yields a novel polyhedral structure.

arxiv-2201-07132.title: Laser Cooling Beyond Rate Equations: Approaches From Quantum Thermodynamics
arxiv-2201-07132.creator: C. N. Murphy, L. Toledo Tude, P. R. Eastham *
arxiv-2201-07132.description: Abstract Solids can be cooled by driving impurity ions with lasers, allowing them to transfer heat from the lattice phonons to the electromagnetic surroundings. This exemplifies a quantum thermal machine, which uses a quantum system as a working medium to transfer heat between reservoirs.

arxiv-2202-09850.title: A Novel Framework for Brain Tumor Detection Based on Convolutional Variational Generative Models
arxiv-2202-09850.creator: Wessam M. Salama, Ahmed Shokry
arxiv-2202-09850.description: Abstract Brain tumor detection can make the difference between life and death. Recently, deep learning-based brain tumor detection techniques have gained attention due to their higher performance. However, obtaining the expected performance of such deep learning-based systems requires large amounts of classified images to train the deep models.

arxiv-2204-13873.title: Multiple Degradation and Reconstruction Network for Single Image Denoising via Knowledge Distillation
arxiv-2204-13873.creator: Juncheng Li, Hanhui Yang, Qiaosi Yi, Faming Fang, Guangwei Gao, Tieyong Zeng, Guixu Zhang
arxiv-2204-13873.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Juncheng Li, Hanhui Yang, Qiaosi Yi, Faming Fang, Guangwei Gao, Tieyong Zeng, Guixu Zhang. Single image denoising (SID) has achieved significant breakthroughs with the development of deep learning. However, the proposed methods are often accompanied by plenty of parameters, which greatly limits their application scenarios. Different from previous works that blindly increase the depth of the network, we explore the degradation mechanism of the noisy image and propose a lightweight Multiple Degradation and Reconstruction Network (MDRN) to progressively remove noise.

arxiv-2301-04341.title: A Meta Path-based Approach for Rumor Detection on Social Media PubID: pubid: 978-1-6654-8027-7/22/$31.00 ©2023 IEEE
arxiv-2301-04341.creator: Bita Azarijoo, Mostafa Salehi, Shaghayegh Najari
arxiv-2301-04341.description: Abstract The prominent role of social media in people’s daily lives has made them more inclined to receive news through social networks than traditional sources. This shift in public behavior has opened doors for some to diffuse fake news on social media; and subsequently cause negative economic, political, and social consequences as well as distrust among the public.

arxiv-2307-09601.title: Modelling reflected polarised light from close-in giant exoplanet WASP-96b using PolHEx (Polarisation of Hot Exoplanets) 2023 Modelling reflected polarised light from close-in giant exoplanet WASP-96b using PolHEx (Polarisation of Hot Exoplanets) – B
arxiv-2307-09601.creator: Katy L. Chubb, Daphne M. Stam, Christiane Helling, Dominic Samra, and Ludmila Carone
arxiv-2307-09601.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Katy L. Chubb, Daphne M. Stam, Christiane Helling, Dominic Samra, and Ludmila Carone. We present the Polarisation of Hot Exoplanets (PolHEx) code for modelling the total flux ( F F ) and degree of linear polarisation ( P P ) of light spectra reflected by close-in, tidally locked exoplanets. We use the output from a global climate model (GCM) combined with a kinetic cloud model of hot Jupiter WASP-96b as a base to investigate effects of atmospheric longitudinal-latitudinal inhomogeneities on these spectra.

arxiv-2312-04565.title: MuRF: Multi-Baseline Radiance Fields
arxiv-2312-04565.creator: Haofei Xu, Anpei Chen, Yuedong Chen, Christos Sakaridis, Yulun Zhang, Marc Pollefeys, Andreas Geiger, Fisher Yu, [3pt] ETH Zurich University of Tübingen, Tübingen AI Center Monash University
arxiv-2312-04565.description: Abstract We present Multi-Baseline Radiance Fields (MuRF), a general feed-forward approach to solving sparse view synthesis under multiple different baseline settings (small and large baselines, and different number of input views). To render a target novel view, we discretize the 3D space into planes parallel to the target image plane, and accordingly construct a target view frustum volume.

arxiv-2401-01756.title: Fuzzy Logic Controller Design for Mobile Robot Outdoor Navigation
arxiv-2401-01756.description: Abstract Many researchers around the world are researching to get control solutions that enhance robots’ ability to navigate in dynamic environments autonomously. However, until these days robots have limited capability and many navigation tasks on Earth and other planets have been difficult so far.

arxiv-2404-10489.title: Computation of the solution for the 2D acoustic pulse propagation
arxiv-2404-10489.creator: P.A. Bakhvalov
arxiv-2404-10489.description: Abstract We consider the 2D acoustic system with the Gaussian pulse as the initial data. This case was proposed at the first Workshop on benchmark problems in computational aeroacoustics, and it is commonly used for the verification of numerical methods.

arxiv-2505-07698.title: A Likelihood Ratio Framework for Highly Motivated Subdominant Signals
arxiv-2505-07698.creator: S. Ansarifard
arxiv-2505-07698.description: Abstract In particle physics and cosmology, distinguishing subtle new physics signals from established backgrounds is a fundamental and persistent challenge for phenomenologists. This paper discuss a simple and robust statistical framework to evaluate the compatibility of highly motivated (HM) theoretical models with the residuals of experimental results, focusing on scenarios where the data appear consistent with background predictions.

arxiv-2509-19543.title: Analytical analysis of the spin wave dispersion in the cycloidal spin structures under the influence of magneto-electric coupling
arxiv-2509-19543.creator: Pavel A. Andreev
arxiv-2509-19543.description: Abstract Spin waves and coupling of the spin waves with electromagnetic waves are considered in the multiferroic materials with the electric dipole moment proportional to the scalar product of spins. Dispersion dependence for the spin waves propagating as the perturbation of the equilibrium state described by spin cycloid is found.

arxiv-2511-15870.title: AquaSentinel: Next-Generation AI System Integrating Sensor Networks for Urban Underground Water Pipeline Anomaly Detection via Collaborative MoE-LLM Agent Architecture
arxiv-2511-15870.creator: Qiming Guo, Bishal Khatri, Wenbo Sun, Jinwen Tang, Hua Zhang, Wenlu Wang
arxiv-2511-15870.description: Abstract Underground pipeline leaks and infiltrations pose significant threats to water security and environmental safety. Traditional manual inspection methods provide limited coverage and delayed response, often missing critical anomalies. This paper proposes AquaSentinel, a novel physics-informed AI system for real-time anomaly detection in urban underground water pipeline networks.

pmc-11348905.title: Simplifying the Centrolene buckleyi complex (Amphibia: Anura: Centrolenidae): a taxonomic review and description of two new species
pmc-11348905.creator: Daniela Franco-Mena, Ignacio De la Riva, Mateo A. Vega-Yánez, Paul Székely, Luis Amador, Diego Batallas, Juan P. Reyes-Puig, Diego F. Cisneros-Heredia, Khristian Venegas-Valencia, Sandra P. Galeano, Jaime Culebras, Juan M. Guayasamin
pmc-11348905.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Centrolenidae is a Neotropical family widely distributed in Central and South America, with its species richness concentrated in the tropical Andes. Several taxonomic problems have been identified within this family, mostly related to species with broad geographic distributions. In this study, we assessed and redefined the species boundaries of the Centrolene buckleyi species complex, and formally described two new species from the Andes of Ecuador. These new taxa are recognized by a combination of morphometric, osteological, acoustic, and genetic data.

pmc-11534827.title: Association of Maternity Leave Characteristics and Postpartum Depressive Symptoms among Women in New York
pmc-11534827.creator: Hannah K Hecht, Angela-Maithy N Nguyen, Kim G Harley
pmc-11534827.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThe United States is the only high-income country without a comprehensive national maternity leave policy guaranteeing paid, job-projected leave. The current study examined associations between maternity leave characteristics (duration of leave, payment status of leave) and postpartum depressive symptoms.MethodsThis study used a sample of 3,515 postpartum women from the New York City and New York State Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) from 2016 to 2019.

pmc-11536775.title: Quality of family planning counseling and associated factors among reproductive age women who are current contraceptive users at Dessie town health facilities east Amhara, 2023
pmc-11536775.creator: Nigusie Abebaw, Berihun Haile, Amare Workie, Wondwosen Mebratu, Molla Getie
pmc-11536775.description: BackgroundThe role of counseling in Family Planning is to care a woman in navigating the process of choosing a contraceptive method that will allow her to fulfill her family planning goals and exercise her reproductive health rights. The effectiveness and appropriateness of family planning counselling play a crucial role in a client’s decision-making process regarding contraception.

pmc-11692325.title: USING LATENT CLASS GROWTH ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY SUBGROUPS OF OLDER ADULTS WITH SHARED TRAJECTORIES OF FRAILTY STATUS
pmc-11692325.creator: Hillary Spangler, Wenyi Xie, David Lynch, Feng-Chang Lin, John Batsis
pmc-11692325.description: BackgroundFrailty is a geriatric syndrome with significant clinical heterogeneity among older adults. Identifying groups experiencing different frailty trajectories is critical for identifying those at high risk of frailty progression and prevention. MethodsWe used data from the National Health and Aging Trend Study (2011-2020), a cohort of Medicare beneficiaries >65 years. Individuals were categorized using Fried’s frailty phenotype.

pmc-11699203.title: Estimation of GHGs emission from traditional kilns charcoal production in northwestern Ethiopia: Implications on climate change
pmc-11699203.creator: Biruk Belay, Dawit Diriba, Feyera Senbeta
pmc-11699203.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Rural areas in Ethiopia serve as the primary source of charcoal for urban populations, mainly produced using traditional kilns. However, this traditional method significantly contributes to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, exacerbating climate change and deforestation. While banning charcoal production is not currently feasible in Ethiopia because of the lack of affordable alternative energy sources (fuel), improving the efficiency of the traditional production system can mitigate the climate impact caused by charcoal production.

pmc-12420699.title: What is the preferred mesh placement in primary ventral hernia repair? An international survey of 442 surgeons
pmc-12420699.creator: Usamah Ahmed, Jacob Rosenberg, Sarfaraz Jalil Baig, Sujith Wijerathne, Wah Yang, Shuqing Li, Jason Joe Baker
pmc-12420699.description: PurposePrimary ventral hernia repair is a common elective procedure; however, mesh placement practices vary widely, and there is limited evidence to guide optimal placement. This international study examined surgeons’ preferences and considerations regarding mesh placement in elective primary ventral hernia repair.MethodsWe conducted an international cross-sectional survey targeting surgeons experienced in primary ventral hernia repair.

pmc-12653246.title: Investigation of the Robustness and Transferability of Adversarial Patches in Multi-View Infrared Target Detection
pmc-12653246.creator: Qing Zhou, Zhongchen Zhou, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Wei Luo, Feng Xiao, Sijia Xia, Chunjia Zhu, Long Wang
pmc-12653246.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper proposes a novel adversarial patch-generation method for infrared images, focusing on enhancing the robustness and transferability of infrared adversarial patches. To improve the flexibility and diversity of the generation process, a Bernoulli random dropout strategy is adopted. The loss function integrates multiple components, including target hiding loss, smoothing loss, structural similarity loss, and patch pixel value loss, ensuring that the generated patches maintain low texture complexity and natural visual features.

pmc-13302329.title: Polarity-dependent repolarization during LBBAP across conduction phenotypes
pmc-13302329.creator: A D'amico, E Cristiano, B Ignatiuk, M Renda, E Bia, M Nardin, M Parrinello, G Albano, L Giroletti, A Graniero, A Agnino, R Rainone, E Celentano
pmc-13302329.description: BackgroundLeft bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is emerging as a viable alternative to traditional right ventricular pacing, as it facilitates more natural ventricular activation. Nonetheless, the impact of LBBAP on ventricular repolarization, especially concerning pacing polarity and pre-existing conduction disorders, has not been extensively explored.

pmc-13392607.title: Disparate immunity proteins independently inactivate an antibacterial nuclease toxin
pmc-13392607.creator: Y Vivian Liu, Jake Colautti, Youngchang Kim, John C Whitney
pmc-13392607.description: Bacteria secrete a diverse arsenal of protein toxins that inhibit the growth of competing species. To avoid self-intoxication, antibacterial toxins are encoded alongside cognate immunity proteins that typically bind to and occlude a toxin’s active site, thus neutralizing its activity. Multiple immunity proteins rarely target the same toxin, reflecting the strong coevolution between toxins and their immunity factors.
